answer: Latency-signed relay slots. Each identity must hold a distinct physical relay slot, earned by completing timed round-trips through an assigned server path (e.g., wharf node to canyon node). The falcon test: a challenge packet must return within a measured window, proving the node occupies real, non-parallel time. Clones can't share one slot because simultaneous challenges split response latency, flagging duplication. An attacker cloning N identities pays N concurrent hardware clocks plus N real round-trip paths, scaling linearly in physical infrastructure and time, not capital.
